q: A PDA accepts w by empty stack when…
options: it reads all of w and the stack is completely empty
it reads all of w and only Z₀ is left
it reaches a final state at any point
the stack becomes empty before the input ends
explain: N(P) = { w | (q₀, w, Z₀) ⊢* (q, ε, ε) }. The input must be used up, and the stack must be truly empty, Z₀ included. The state does not matter.

q: A PDA accepts w by final state when…
options: it reads all of w and ends in a state of F, whatever the stack holds
it reads all of w and the stack is empty
it enters a final state after reading any prefix of w
explain: L(P) = { w | (q₀, w, Z₀) ⊢* (q, ε, γ), q ∈ F }. The remaining stack γ can be anything.

q: For nondeterministic PDAs, acceptance by final state and acceptance by empty stack define the same class of languages.
explain: True. Each kind of PDA can be converted into the other, so both give exactly the context-free languages.

q: When converting an empty-stack PDA into a final-state PDA, why is a new bottom marker X₀ pushed under Z₀?
options: So the new PDA can tell when the old stack has become empty, and then jump to a final state
explain: When X₀ appears on top, the old PDA's stack is empty. That is exactly when the old PDA would accept, so an ε-move to the new final state is taken.

q: When converting a final-state PDA into an empty-stack PDA, what does the new 'drain' state do?
options: Pops every remaining stack symbol using ε-moves
Reads the rest of the input
explain: From each old final state an ε-move goes to the drain state, which empties the stack, the new marker included.

q: Why is a new bottom marker also needed in the final-state → empty-stack conversion?
options: Otherwise the old PDA might empty its stack in a non-final state and wrongly accept
Otherwise the PDA cannot read input
Because empty-stack PDAs need two start states
explain: The new marker X₀ can only be popped by the drain state. That way, the stack is empty only when the old PDA has really reached a final state.

q: For deterministic PDAs, acceptance by empty stack is as powerful as acceptance by final state.
explain: False. A DPDA that accepts by empty stack can only accept prefix-free languages, because it cannot continue once the stack is empty. {a, aa} shows the gap.

q: The PDA has δ(q₀, a, Z₀) = (q₀, AZ₀), δ(q₀, a, A) = (q₀, AA), δ(q₀, b, A) = (q₁, ε), δ(q₁, b, A) = (q₁, ε) and δ(q₁, ε, Z₀) = (q₁, ε), and accepts by empty stack. Which strings does it accept?
explain: It accepts exactly aⁿbⁿ with n ≥ 1. In aababb, an a comes while the PDA is in q₁, where there is no move on a. In abb, the second b finds Z₀ on top, and there is no move for that either.

q: Which language can a DPDA accept by final state but not by empty stack?
explain: 'a' is a prefix of 'aa'. After accepting 'a' with an empty stack, a DPDA has no stack symbol left to make a move on the second a.

q: Is a stack holding only Z₀ an empty stack?
options: No: Z₀ is a symbol, and empty means no symbols at all
explain: Empty-stack acceptance needs Z₀ popped as well. Many PDAs end with an ε-move that pops Z₀ for exactly this reason.
